texts.textentryhtml:
Imperial Court Library (Kaiserliche Hofbibliothek), Vienna (originally as part of Rembrandt print album, volume HB69.2, page 9); transferred after WWI (~1920) to the Albertina, Vienna, Austria, and deaccessioned as a duplicate between 1922 and 1947 [1]. Gilbert S. McClintock (1886–1959); gifted to the Princeton University Art Museum, 1957.

[1] Lugt 5g stamp on verso was used from 1922 to 1947. This print, however, does not appear in any of the Albertina deaccessioning sales catalogues by C.G. Boerner in Leipzig in 1922, 1924, 1925, 1932.
texts.remarks: Via correspondence between Ronni Baer's student Kendal Lloyd and Dr. Eva Michel, 10-11-25: "Following the inscription on our print, it was originally stored in volume HB69.2, page 9, in the Albertina. This volume containing parts of Rembrandt’s printed oeuvre was originally part of the Imperial Court Library („Hofbibliothek“, short „HB“), but the prints of the Court Library were integrated in the Albertina after First World War and the end of monarchy in Austria. I checked the volume HB 69.2, p.9: unfortunately there is no note about the fate of the print. The volume is now nearly empty, as some prints might have been mounted separately and are still in the Albertina, and some might have been sold as „doublettes“ between the First and the Second World war. My colleague Alex Pointner was so kind to check the lists of sold doublettes, but he was not able to find the Rembrandt-print there. I am very sorry that I cannot tell you any more on the provenance."
